financial-asset.def: A claim on money or future income, such as money, a bond or a share of stock. Bonds are loans to the issuer; stocks are shares of ownership. Liquidity is how easily an asset becomes money without losing value.

bond-price-rate.def: The prices of existing bonds move opposite to market interest rates. A bond pays a fixed amount, so when new bonds pay more, buyers pay less for an old one.

interest-rate.def: The price of borrowing: what a borrower pays each year for the use of money, as a percent of the amount borrowed. To a lender it is the reward for lending.
